title: Sturton by Stow R.5676 Memorial
crew_summary: 9 crew — 8 killed including pilot Flg Off. Sydney Rhys Jones

external_narratives.summary: Registry entry for the Lancaster R5676 memorial at Lancaster Farm, Sturton by Stow. The memorial was commissioned by farm owner Jacqueline Gorman and designed by her son John Gorman.
external_narratives.key_details: Memorial located on the wall at the entrance to Lancaster Farm on Tillbridge Road. Privately commissioned memorial on the crash site.
external_narratives.link_description: Lancaster R5676 Memorial's registry entry: a tribute from Jacqueline Gorman to her son John Gorman at Sturton by Stow.

external_narratives.summary: RAF Commands archive record for Flying Officer Sydney Rhys Jones and the crew of Lancaster R5676 from 1660 HCU. The Lancaster broke up in flight at 1005 hours on 12 February 1943, with the starboard wing failing first.
external_narratives.key_details: Aircraft suffered structural failure — starboard wing broke away in flight. Crashed at Oldfield's Farm, 8 miles NW of Lincoln. Crew of eight included Fg Off Jones (age 25), Sgt Raeside (age 26), Fg Off Hoy (age 31), Sgt Westwood (age 22), Sgt Jackson (age 23), Fg Off Krish (age 26), F/Sgt Kennedy (age 20), and Sgt Redfern (age 23).
external_narratives.link_description: RAF Commands archive record for Flying Officer Sydney Rhys Jones and crew of Lancaster R5676, detailing aircraft breakdown mid-flight in 1943.

external_narratives.summary: Photograph and description of the memorial to the crew of Lancaster R5676 at Sturton by Stow, showing the stone memorial on the wall of Lancaster Farm.
external_narratives.key_details: Memorial is publicly visible on the roadside wall of the farm. The farm itself was renamed 'Lancaster Farm' in honour of the crew.

narrative: At 1005 on 12 February 1943, Lancaster R5676 of 1660 Heavy Conversion Unit, based at Swinderby, suffered a structural failure when the starboard wing broke away in flight. The aircraft crashed at Oldfield's Farm, approximately 8 miles north-west of Lincoln, near Sturton by Stow. Eight of the nine crew were killed: Flying Officer Sydney Rhys Jones (pilot, aged 25), Sergeant W.T. Raeside (aged 26), Flying Officer Stanley Hoy (air bomber, aged 31), Sergeant J. Westwood (aged 22), Sergeant T.H. Jackson (aged 23), Flying Officer F.M. Krish (aged 26), Flight Sergeant Gerald 'Bunny' Kennedy RCAF (air gunner, aged 20), and Leading Aircraftman E.R. Redfern (aged 23). The farm on the crash site was subsequently renamed Lancaster Farm.
crew_note: Crew roles corrected per Facebook post by Nick Taylor (RAF Bomber Command Memorials group): F/O Sydney Rhys Jones was the pilot; F/Sgt Gerald Kennedy RCAF was the air gunner (not the pilot); F/O Stanley Hoy was British (not Canadian). The previous entry had Kennedy listed as pilot and Hoy listed as Canadian — both were wrong.

crew.name: Stanley Hoy
crew.nationality_note: British — corrected from Canadian. Buried with his brother at Hull Eastern Cemetery.

memorial_details:
Memorial Unveiling (2003-05-12): Commissioned by Jacqueline Gorman, designed and made by her son John Gorman. The memorial consists of an allegory of a Lancaster bomber inset into a railing on the top of the wall, below which is a blue laminated plate with white lettering.

The stone memorial on its roadside wall was commissioned by farm owner Jacqueline Gorman and designed by her son John Gorman; it was unveiled on 12 May 2003.
community_connection: The memorial is maintained by Sturton by Stow Parish Council.
